header.name: Introduction to Machine Learning
header.description: This introductory course on Machine Learning covers foundational concepts, algorithms, and practical workflows for building ML systems. Students will study supervised, unsupervised, probabilistic, linear, kernel-based, ensemble, and basic neural network methods. The course includes theory and programming assignments using real and simulated datasets, with emphasis on preprocessing, model training, evaluation, error analysis, and reproducibility. It also provides brief exposure to representation learning, pretrained models, and responsible ML, while preparing students for courses such as Deep Learning, NLP, and Computer Vision.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Students should be able to explain the mathematical, probabilistic, and statistical foundations underlying core machine learning methods.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Students should be able to formulate real-world problems as machine learning tasks, select suitable models, and train them using appropriate optimization and evaluation procedures.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Students should be able to implement and use standard supervised, unsupervised, and representation-learning methods using modern machine learning tools and libraries.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Students should be able to analyze the performance, limitations, failure modes, and ethical implications of machine learning models, including issues of bias, robustness, generalization, and responsible deployment.

lecture_topics: Mathematical Refresher for ML: multivariable functions, partial derivatives, gradients, Jacobian, Hessian, and unconstrained nonlinear optimization
Examples may include MSE, BCE, and gradient-based optimization
weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: Python/NumPy tutorial on vectors, matrices, gradients, and simple loss-surface visualization. Implement gradient descent for a simple quadratic/MSE objective.

lecture_topics: Probability and Statistics for ML: conditional probability, Bayes’ theorem, random variables, multivariate Gaussian, covariance matrix, MLE, and MAP estimation
weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: Probability and statistics exercises using Python; estimation of Gaussian parameters from data; simple MLE/MAP examples.

lecture_topics: Introduction to Machine Learning: types of learning problems, supervised/unsupervised learning, risk minimization framework, empirical risk, generalization, and basic ML pipeline
Linear Regression: closed-form solution and gradient-based training
weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: Implement linear regression using both closed-form solution and gradient descent; compare training loss and test performance.

lecture_topics: Linear Models and Regularization: linear regression, ridge regression, lasso regression, logistic regression, sigmoid function, MLE/MAP view, and gradient descent
weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: Implement ridge/lasso/logistic regression using scikit-learn; study the effect of regularization on model weights and performance.

lecture_topics: Practical Aspects of ML: Train/validation/test splits, cross-validation, evaluation metrics, bias-variance trade-off, overfitting/underfitting, error analysis, model selection, and basics of calibration and uncertainty, including confidence scores
weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: Build a complete evaluation pipeline: train/validation/test split, cross-validation, metric selection, confusion matrix/error analysis, and basic calibration plot/confidence-score analysis.

lecture_topics: Data, Features, and ML Pipelines: Data preprocessing, feature engineering, feature selection, leakage, ablation analysis, reproducibility, and experiment tracking
weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: End-to-end ML pipeline using scikit-learn: preprocessing, feature transformations, pipeline construction, ablation study, and reproducible experiment logging.

lecture_topics: Probabilistic and Non-parametric Methods: Naive Bayes as a generative classifier, KNN as a non-parametric classifier, decision boundaries, assumptions, strengths, and limitations
weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: Mid-sem Project Presentation: Students are expected to present around 40–50% progress on their course project. The presentation should cover the problem formulation, dataset details, preprocessing completed, baseline model(s), initial experimental results, evaluation plan, challenges faced, and next steps for improving the model and completing the project.

lecture_topics: Tree-based Models and Ensembles: decision trees, bagging, random forests, boosting, gradient boosting trees, and practical comparison with linear models
weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: Probabilistic and Non-parametric Methods: Naive Bayes as a generative classifier, KNN as a non-parametric classifier, decision boundaries, assumptions, strengths, and limitations.

lecture_topics: Support Vector Machines and Kernels: linear SVM, margin maximization, primal and dual formulation, kernel trick, and Kernel SVM
weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: Implement SVMs using linear and kernel settings; visualize margins and decision boundaries; study the effect of C, kernel choice, and kernel parameters.

lecture_topics: Neural Networks as ML Models: perceptron, activation functions, multilayer perceptrons, loss functions, backpropagation, and basic neural network training
weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: Implement a small MLP using PyTorch/TensorFlow; train using backpropagation; study the effect of activation functions, learning rate, batch size, and overfitting.

lecture_topics: Representation Learning and Feature Embeddings: Classical and learned representations, dimensionality reduction methods such as PCA, feature embeddings, pretrained/foundation models
weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: Apply PCA for dimensionality reduction and visualization; use pretrained embeddings/features for a downstream classification task; compare handcrafted, PCA-based, and pretrained representations.

lecture_topics: Clustering and density-based unsupervised learning methods, including k-means clustering and Gaussian Mixture Models
weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: Implement k-means and GMM clustering; compare cluster quality using internal/external metrics; visualize clusters and discuss sensitivity to initialization and number of clusters.

lecture_topics: FAT Aspects of ML and Industry Lecture
Fairness, accountability, and transparency in ML, including bias, interpretability, robustness, evaluation limitations, model misuse, and deployment concerns
Industry-invited lecture to expose students to practical ML workflows, real-world constraints, and responsible deployment practices
weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: Final project presentation: end-to-end ML solution, preprocessing, model design, training/validation/testing, quantitative comparison, error analysis, limitations, and responsible-use considerations.

Scikit-learn, PyTorch/TensorFlow, and related official documentation, as needed for tutorials and assignments.
